newsitem.title: UK: Britain springs surprise with $2.0 billion FRN.
newsitem.headline: Britain springs surprise with $2.0 billion FRN.

text.p: Britain caught the primary market unawares early on Thursday in Europe with the launch of a $2.0 billion five-year FRN, its second Eurobond in two months.

"As far as the market is concerned, this is a surprise. That's the way the Bank (of England) prefers to do it," said one new issues manager at a British bank close to the deal. There was speculation recently Britain was lining up another jumbo deal but rumoured terms were vague. It launched a $2.0 billion five-year fixed-rate deal on July 15 as partial refinancing of a $4.0 billion FRN being repaid on September 30.
Today's deal, which will be callable at par on coupon dates from October 1999, was reoffered at the 99.745 issue price for a margin of 19 basis points below three-month LIBOR.
The Bank of Engand said the issue was for routine debt management purposes and the proceeds would complete the refinancing of the $4.0 billion FRN.
The new paper will pay 12.5 basis points below three-month LIBID, the same as the maturing paper.
BZW was bookrunner and joint lead manager with HSBC Markets and NatWest Markets also joint-lead managers.

Britain's previous deal in July was its first Eurobond since 1992. It was priced at a five basis points yield spread over U.S. Treasuries via Goldman Sachs International and SBC Warburg and was universally judged a storming success.
The Bank of England said at the time the proceeds would be used to refinance part of the $4.0 billion FRN and that there was no need to refinance the other $2.0 billion.
